item.title: The future of optical networks: Evolution and imperatives
item.description: How can we unlock the full potential of optical networks? Critical innovations are emerging, but closing technical, commercial, and operational gaps will require focused industry collaboration and forward-thinking strategy from all parties.

item.title: Photonics Hot List: January 23, 2026
item.description: In this episode: Fluorescence imaging follows drugs’ path in the body, business moves for four companies, and AI computing at light speed.

item.title: Radio telescopes benefit from ultraprecise optical frequency combs
item.description: Researchers apply the precision of optical frequency combs to radio telescopes to synchronize the observation timing and phase of faint cosmic signals—and lay the foundation for multiple distant radio telescopes to operate as a single giant telescope.

item.title: Tunable diode lasers: A path to practical quantum systems
item.description: By leveraging tunable diode lasers and a synergetic combination of public and private investments and partnerships, the industry can speed development and adoption of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) technologies for the emerging quantum market.

item.title: Quantum switch?
item.description: Researchers discover a single quantum parameter—the size of its spin—acts as a switch that flips its magnetism. This discovery offers a new way to think about how quantum states can be controlled within complex materials.

item.title: The programmable optics revolution
item.description: Active metasurfaces are ushering in a new era of programmable optics.

item.title: Photonics Hot List: January 30, 2026
item.description: In this episode: A microscopy approach could advance space exploration, this week's photonics business moves, and our SPIE Photonics West 2026 recap.

item.title: Ultrafast light switch for optical data components
item.description: Researchers move a step closer to femtosecond switching of ‘light by light’ for photonic computing based on polaritons.

item.title: Nonlinear metasurfaces convert infrared light to visible
item.description: A new nonlinear metasurface retains nonlocal, high-Q enhancement while preserving subwavelength per-pixel phase control—and it’s a big step toward on-chip visible/ultraviolet light sources, LiDAR beam steering, quantum light generation, optical signal processing, and polarization-encoded computing.
